reviews.title: ⭐ 1 Star — Extremely Disappointing Treatment of a Small Business
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with how Invoice2go handled my account. I signed up to use this service for my business, provided the information and documents that were requested, and then my account was suddenly deactivated and permanently closed.

What makes this worse is that Invoice2go told me that all pending payments were canceled and/or refunded, but when I asked why my business was being denied service, I was told they were unable to provide any further information regarding the decision.

That is unacceptable when you’re dealing with a small business that depends on invoicing and payment processing. If there was an issue with my account, documentation, verification, or anything else, I should at least be given a meaningful explanation or an opportunity to correct it.

I am posting this review because normal support has not provided me with an answer. I would like someone from Invoice2go management, account review, or the appropriate escalation department to contact me directly and actually review what happened to my account.

I am willing to update this review if Invoice2go reaches out, explains the situation, and makes a genuine effort to resolve it.

reviews.title: No support for growth
reviews.text:
As a generator installation company, we have used Invoice2go for over a year and have grown significantly during that time. While the platform itself has been helpful, we have encountered a major issue with payment processing limits.

Our business regularly invoices approximately $15,000 per generator installation, yet our monthly payout limit remains capped at $50,000. This means our funds are frequently held back, creating unnecessary cash flow challenges and forcing us to wait extended periods to access money that rightfully belongs to our business.

What has been most disappointing is the lack of resolution despite multiple attempts to address the issue. We have submitted requests to increase our payout limits, provided banking references, and even had our bank verify our financial standing and available funds across multiple accounts. Unfortunately, none of these efforts resulted in any meaningful action or communication.

For a growing business, reliable access to earned funds is critical. The inability to increase reasonable payout limits, combined with the lack of responsiveness, has been extremely frustrating and has negatively impacted our experience with the platform.

I hope Invoice2go will improve its support process and provide more flexibility for established businesses that have demonstrated a strong payment history and financial stability.

reviews.title: 13 years… time to switch.
reviews.text:
13 year user here. This app was by far the best when I first started using it. Just enough features for a small business to use for basic invoicing and expense tracking.  You could export reports right from the app, and expense tracking was good. 

Invoice2go is probably still a great fit more many people. I just don’t think it’s me anymore. 

I’ve switched to the monthly subscription, so I can back up my data, and make the move to something else. Such a shame.  Just simple things would change it all for me. But it’ll never happen, based on the last 6 years or so of waiting. 

I’ve been waiting for many years for some basic improvements. A feature removed long ago was a very simple “cost of goods” system, that allowed you to bill an expense to an invoice, and when viewing the expenses you’d see the “tagged invoice” in the reports. 
That feature was removed, and eventually replaced with “projects”.  Something that over complicated the original feature. 

But also, the reporting.  Whether your using the app, or the website version, to get a report you have to; select the report (which most have current year, but if you want 2025 you have to select “custom” and do the date range) then click export, which then sends a link to your email, which then bounces you back to your browser for download, then you can open it. Talk about annoying.

reviews.title: My Recent Experience With Invoice2go’s Payment System
reviews.text:
After more than a decade using Invoice2go to manage invoicing for my restoration business, I have always appreciated the platform for its practicality and ease of use. However, I recently encountered a situation that raised serious concerns about their new credit-card processing system and the quality of their customer support.

Invoice2go has recently resumed accepting credit-card payments through a third-party processor, Bill.com. Unfortunately, this change created unexpected complications that affected both me and my client. One of my customers did not recognize the charge from Bill.com on her American Express statement, and she disputed the transaction—even though the payment was legitimately made for services I provided.

Once I learned of the issue, I immediately clarified with my client that Bill.com was simply Invoice2go’s new processor. She confirmed the payment was valid and even sent a written statement explaining that she had authorized the charge. I forwarded her letter to Invoice2go, expecting a quick resolution.

Instead, the process became increasingly frustrating. Invoice2go refused to release the funds and requested an additional letter directly from my client’s American Express account—an unreasonable and inconvenient requirement for both my client and for me. Despite my effort to cooperate, I was eventually forced to obtain a copy of the original transaction directly from my client’s AMEX statement and send it to Invoice2go as further proof.
